content.thinking: Since Grace isn't an authorised party, I shouldn't disclose any account details to her—no balance, no status. Instead I can offer to relay a message to the tenant and ask for their consent to share anything further, and note that any third-party payment would just need the account reference, not balance info. I'll log this call, then reach out to the tenant by email explaining who called and checking if they're okay given she mentioned being "very down," possibly flagging Samaritans as a resource if appropriate, while being mindful I have no way to message Grace back directly.

arguments.party_name: Grace (claims to be Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller said she is tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Caller's DOB for tenant (2 Nov) is also not a match for the record, and knowing address/DOB is not authority anyway. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payment history, contact details, not even confirming whether there are arrears). Offered: pass a message to Jonah; Jonah can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; if she wants to pay, a third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address, without being told the balance. Will tell Jonah by email who called.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today asking about your rent and for your phone number. We shared nothing about your account or contact details, as we have no consent from you on file. She said she'd like to help. If you're happy for us to talk to her, reply to let us know in writing and we can add her as an authorised contact. If not, we'll leave it as it is. She can also pay towards rent by quoting the property address, without us telling her any balance. If you're feeling low, Samaritans are free on 116 123 any time. We'll look out for your reply and follow up by email in a few days if we haven't heard.

content.thinking: Since Grace isn't an authorised party, I shouldn't disclose any account details to her—no balance, no status. Instead I can offer to relay a message to the tenant and ask for their consent to share anything further, and note that any third-party payment would just need the account reference, not balance info. I'll log this call, then reach out to the tenant by email explaining who called and checking if they're okay given she mentioned being "very down," possibly flagging Samaritans as a resource if appropriate, while being mindful I have no way to message Grace back directly.

arguments.party_name: Grace (claims to be Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller said she is tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Caller's DOB for tenant (2 Nov) is also not a match for the record, and knowing address/DOB is not authority anyway. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payment history, contact details, not even confirming whether there are arrears). Offered: pass a message to Jonah; Jonah can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; if she wants to pay, a third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address, without being told the balance. Will tell Jonah by email who called.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today asking about your rent and for your phone number. We shared nothing about your account or contact details, as we have no consent from you on file. She said she'd like to help. If you're happy for us to talk to her, reply to let us know in writing and we can add her as an authorised contact. If not, we'll leave it as it is. She can also pay towards rent by quoting the property address, without us telling her any balance. If you're feeling low, Samaritans are free on 116 123 any time. We'll look out for your reply and follow up by email in a few days if we haven't heard.
